analysis.investment_thesis: IXIGO is a commoditized OTA business trading at 133x earnings with a declining net profit (₹73 Cr → ₹60 Cr despite 39% revenue growth) and an ROE of just 9.74% — far below the 15% minimum I demand. At this price, I'm being asked to pay a luxury price for a tourist-class business in a fiercely competitive market where IRCTC holds the real moat.
key_strengths: Asset-light model with 81.74% gross margin and near-zero debt (D/E: 0.04), generating ₹118 Cr FCF in FY25
Strong revenue trajectory — ₹914 Cr in FY25 vs ₹40 Cr in 2019, with diversified platforms (ixigo, Confirmtkt, AbhiBus) targeting India's price-sensitive traveler
Operating CF turned sharply positive in FY25 (₹122 Cr) after years of cash burn, showing early operational maturity
key_risks: No durable moat — OTA is a commodity; travelers routinely compare across MakeMyTrip, EaseMyTrip, Cleartrip with zero switching cost
IRCTC owns the actual train ticketing infrastructure and can squeeze OTA margins at will — ixigo's core segment is structurally exposed
Extreme valuation (P/E 133x, EV/EBITDA 119x) leaves no margin of safety; even at forward P/E of 57x, profitability must sustain explosive growth with no stumble
red_flags: Net profit fell from ₹73 Cr (FY24) to ₹60 Cr (FY25) despite 39% revenue growth — operating leverage is not materializing
Other Income was ₹39 Cr in FY24 and ₹23 Cr in FY25; strip it out and core operating profitability is razor-thin (operating income: ₹72 Cr)
Recent IPO (June 2024) — classic post-listing euphoria pricing; FII ownership at 64% means institutional momentum, not business value, is driving the price
Investing outflow of -₹203 Cr in FY25 with financing inflow of +₹104 Cr signals ongoing capital hunger despite claimed profitability
analysis.detailed_analysis:
IXIGO operates in a segment I simply don't find investable at any reasonable price: a digitally-mediated travel marketplace where the product is identical across competitors and the customer's only loyalty is to the cheapest fare. The gross margin of 81.74% looks wonderful until you realize it's the nature of software-distribution economics — it says nothing about pricing power. When IRCTC can change its API fees or commission structure, ixigo has no recourse. That's the opposite of a moat; it's a dependency. ROE of 9.74% tells me the business earns less on equity than a good fixed deposit, and the profit actually shrank year-over-year despite 39% revenue growth — that's a troubling signal about cost structure and competitive intensity.

The valuation is simply unjustifiable by any framework I use. At 133x trailing earnings and 119x EV/EBITDA, the market is pricing in a decade of flawless execution in one of India's most brutally competitive digital sectors. I've seen this story before — exciting growth, thin margins, no moat, and a premium price that assumes nothing ever goes wrong. Charlie would remind me: invert, always invert. What does this stock need to go right? Everything. What could go wrong? Plenty — a regulatory change at IRCTC, MakeMyTrip cutting commissions, or simply a demand slowdown. I would not buy this business at ₹179, and frankly, I'm not sure what price would make it attractive given the structural absence of a durable competitive advantage.
